# OVERVIEW

This Master Data Dictionary summarises all surveys, assessments, and standardised (clinical) scales included in the NCMH data repository.

## Surveys/ Assessments

```{r, echo = FALSE}

survey_names <- read.csv("../Processed_Data/Master_Data_Dictionary_SurveyNames.csv")
colnames(survey_names) <- c("Survey/ Assessment Name", "Survey/ Assessment Grouping")

```

Below is a table of all **`r nrow(survey_names)`** NCMH surveys/ assessments, and their respective groupings. 

This table may be useful when searching for specific datasets within the Master Data Dictionary. 

```{r, echo = FALSE}

datatable(survey_names, 
          rownames = FALSE,
          class = "compact stripe hover",
          options = list(searching = TRUE,
                         searchHighlight = TRUE,
                         search = list(regex = TRUE, 
                                       caseInsensitive = TRUE),
                         pageLength = 10,
                         lengthMenu = c(10, 20, 50, 100),
                         language = list(search = 'Search:'),
                         initComplete = JS(
                           "function(settings, json) {",
                        "$(this.api().table().header()).css({'background-color':
                           '#7B0D1E', 'color': '#fff'});",
                           "$(this.api().table().container()).css({'font-size':
                           '100%'});",
                           "}")
                         )) 

```

## Standardised Scales

```{r, echo = FALSE}

stan_scales <- as.data.frame(read.csv("../Processed_Data/Master_Data_Dictionary_ScalesTotal.csv"))
stan_scales <- stan_scales %>% arrange(desc(Frequency))
colnames(stan_scales) <- c("Standardised Scale Name", "Frequency")

```

Below is a table of all **`r nrow(stan_scales)`** standardised (clinical) scales used in NCMH research, as well as the number of times (frequency) each standardised scale has been used across different NCMH surveys/ assessments.

## Complete Variable List (Variable Search)

```{r, echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, error = FALSE}

dd_complete <- read.csv("../Processed_Data/Master_Data_Dictionary_Complete.csv")

# REMOVE NON-UTF8 CHARACTERS
dd_complete <- as.data.frame(lapply(dd_complete, iconv, to = "UTF-8"))

# MODIFY VARIABLES
dd_complete$index <- 1:nrow(dd_complete)
dd_complete$original_variable_name <- NULL

```

The table below includes a total of **`r nrow(dd_complete)` variables**, derived from all NCMH surveys/ assessments included in this Master Data Dictionary.

You may use this table to search for specific variables or questions relevant to your research. The **source** column can also help you identify which surveys/ assessments your desired data is derived from. 

```{r, echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, error = FALSE}

datatable(dd_complete, 
          rownames = FALSE,
          class = "compact stripe hover nowrap",
          options = list(searching = TRUE,
                         searchHighlight = TRUE,
                         search = list(regex = TRUE, 
                                       caseInsensitive = TRUE),
                         pageLength = 10,
                         lengthMenu = c(10, 20, 50, 100),
                         language = list(search = 'Search Variables:'),
                         initComplete = JS(
                           "function(settings, json) {",
                        "$(this.api().table().header()).css({'background-color':
                           '#7B0D1E', 'color': '#fff'});",
                           "$(this.api().table().container()).css({'font-size':
                           '100%'});",
                           "}")
                         )) 

```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

```{r, echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, error = FALSE}

# CREATE TABLE
create_tab <- function(data) { 
  
  datatable(data, 
            rownames = FALSE,
            class = "compact stripe hover nowrap",
            options = list(searching = TRUE,
                           searchHighlight = TRUE,
                           search = list(regex = TRUE, 
                                         caseInsensitive = TRUE),
                           pageLength = 10,
                           lengthMenu = c(10, 20, 50, 100),
                           language = list(search = 'Search Variables:'),
                           initComplete = JS(
                             "function(settings, json) {",
                        "$(this.api().table().header()).css({'background-color':
                             '#7B0D1E', 'color': '#fff'});",
                            "$(this.api().table().container()).css({'font-size':
                             '100%'});",
                             "}")
                           )
            ) 
}

# CSV BUTTON
csv_button <- function(file_path, name, ext){ 
  download_file(path = file_path,
  output_name = name, 
  output_extension = ext,
  button_label = "Download Data Dictionary (CSV)",
  button_type = "info",
  has_icon = TRUE,
  icon = "fa fa-save",
  self_contained = FALSE
  )
}

# PDF BUTTON
pdf_button <- function(file_path, name, ext){ 
  download_file(path = file_path,
  output_name = name, 
  output_extension = ext,
  button_label = "Download Survey/ Assessment PDF",
  button_type = "info",
  has_icon = TRUE,
  icon = "fa fa-save",
  self_contained = FALSE
  )
}

```

# BRIEF ASSESSMENTS

Developed in 2011, participants across the NCMH cohort have been recruited into a variation of the **NCMH Brief Assessment** up until the present day. These assessments act as a gateway into the NCMH cohort and have been used to capture general demographic and psychiatric history information.

## Brief Assessment WMHN

The first iteration of the NCMH Brief Assessment developed when NCMH was previously named the *Welsh Mental Health Network (WMHN)*. This assessment was split into four variations, each of which utilised for different purposes.

### Brief Assessment WMHN - Participant Information

```{r, echo = FALSE}

brief_wmhn_psinfo <- read.csv("../Individual_Surveys/Brief Assessment WMHN - Participant Information/Brief Assessment WMHN - Participant Information.csv")

```

The **Participant Information** version of the assessment was administered to most participants in the NCMH cohort during this recruitment period, collecting details about the participants demographics, medical history, medication, and substance use.

**Total Variables**: `r nrow(brief_wmhn_psinfo %>% group_by(new_variable_name) %>% slice(1))`
<br>**Total Participants**: 5338 
<br>**Recruitment Dates**: Jan 2011 - Dec 2017 
<br>**Recruitment Method**: Participant Self-completed or Researcher Administered 
<br>**Data Collection Method**: Offline (FORMIC)
<br>**Status**: Closed 
<br>**Principal Investigator**: Prof. Ian Jones
<br>**Standardised Scales Included**: None

```{r, echo = FALSE}

# CSV FILE
csv_button(
  file_path = "../Individual_Surveys/Brief Assessment WMHN - Participant Information/Brief Assessment WMHN - Participant Information.csv",
  name = "NCMH Brief Assessment WMHN - Participant Information",
  ext = ".csv"
)

# PDF FILE
pdf_button(
  file_path = "../Individual_Surveys/Brief Assessment WMHN - Participant Information/Brief Assessment WMHN - Participant Information.pdf",
  name = "NCMH Brief Assessment WMHN - Participant Information",
  ext = ".pdf"
)

# TABLE
create_tab(data = brief_wmhn_psinfo)

```

## Brief Assessment Screening

The second iteration of the NCMH Brief Assessment, developed when NCMH became a standalone research organisation. This assessment was split into two variations, both very similar in content with slight variations in the alcohol use and drug consumption questions.

### Brief Assessment Screening (v1)

```{r, echo = FALSE}

brief_screening_v1 <- read.csv("../Individual_Surveys/Brief Assessment Screening (v1)/Brief Assessment Screening (v1).csv")

```

The first version (v1) of the assessment was administered to a small number of NCMH participants during this recruitment period. This collected details about the participants demographics, informant/ next of kin information, family demographics, children, psychiatric history, social factors, treatments, family psychiatric history, physical health, and substance use.

**Total Variables**: `r nrow(brief_screening_v1 %>% group_by(new_variable_name) %>% slice(1))`
<br>**Total Participants**: 1188 
<br>**Recruitment Dates**: Jul 2016 - Nov 2019 
<br>**Recruitment Method**: Participant Self-completed, Parent/ Carer Completed, or Researcher Administered 
<br>**Data Collection Method**: Offline (FORMIC) 
<br>**Status**: Closed 
<br>**Principal Investigator**: Prof. Ian Jones 
<br>**Standardised Scales Included**: None

## Brief Assessment Screening (Other)

Alongside the second iteration of the NCMH Brief Assessment, other variants of the assessment were developed and administered in parallel during the same recruitment period. Each assessment differed slightly in content and target population.

### Brief Assessment NDAU

```{r, echo = FALSE}

brief_ndau <- read.csv("../Individual_Surveys/Brief Assessment NDAU/Brief Assessment NDAU.csv")

```

Administered to small number of participants, this assessment focussed on children with neurodevelopmental disorders as part of the Neurodevelopment Assessment Unit (NDAU) research project. This collected details about the participants and parents' demographics.

# NCMH RESEARCH COMMUNITY

Initiated in 2025, the NCMH Research Community was developed to build on all the research conducted by NCMH in the 14-years prior, with the emphasis on greater participant engagement and a focus on developing an online research community. Starting with a signup survey (developed using pre-existing questions from our **NCMH Brief Assessment**), participants would provide basic demographic and psychiatric history information. Following this, the aim of the research community was to keep participants engaged with regular (6-12-monthly) followup assessments containing questions on relevant research topics.

## Research Community Signup

```{r, echo = FALSE}

rescom_signup <- read.csv("../Individual_Surveys/Research Community Signup/Research Community Signup.csv", fileEncoding = "latin1")

```

This assessment was administered to all new participants entering NCMH, as well as being sent to existing participants to allow for existing data to be refreshed/ updated. This collected details about the participants demographics, psychiatric history, treatments, children, family psychiatric history, treatments, physical health, and substance use.

**Total Variables**: `r nrow(rescom_signup %>% group_by(new_variable_name) %>% slice(1))`
<br>**Total Participants**: 10+ 
<br>**Recruitment Dates**: May 2026 - Present
<br>**Recruitment Method**: Participant Self-completed

# INDEPTH MOOD AND PSYCHOSIS (SCAN) ASSESSMENTS

Developed as a detailed followup assessment to the early versions of the NCMH Brief Assessment, the *indepth* assessment was conducted with a researcher and involved a thorough assessment of the participants psychiatric history. Many questions on the indepth assessments were copied from the **Brief Assessment Screening**, with additional sections being added to validate psychiatric diagnoses using OPCRIT (Operational Criteria Checklist for Psychotic Illness and Affective Illness) scales.

# ADULT QUESTIONNAIRES (AQs)

Developed in 2011, Adult Questionnaires (AQs) were administered to a large proportion of the cohort following the completion of an **NCMH Brief Assessment**. The AQs were largely self-completed assessments which included various standardised clinical scales (e.g. PHQ-9, GAD-7, etc.) and were completed in the participants own time; often sent to participants and returned by post using the address details provided in the Brief Assessment. The AQs covered a wide range of topic, with several variations being developed over time.

# WOMEN'S MENTAL HEALTH ASSESSMENTS

Alongside other assessments within NCMH focussing primarily on women's mental health, the following are centred around reproductive mental health and experiences during the perinatal period (timeframe during pregnancy and ~2 years after birth). Each assessment focussed on different areas of reproductive mental health, for example Premenstrual Dysphoric Disorder (PMDD), Post-partum Psychosis (PP), or mental health more generally in the context of childbirth.

## Mother and Baby Unit (MBU) Assessment

Developed in 2022, this assessment was developed utilising many of the questions and standardised scales used in other NCMH assessments. Recruiting exclusively through systematic methods, researchers from NHS sites containing mother and baby units would administer this assessment to mothers after being admitted. This assessment collected details about the participants demographics, psychiatric history, pregnancy, children, family psychiatric history, physical health, substance use, work and social adjustment, depression and anxiety symptoms, life events/ trauma experiences, medication use, sleep quality, and wellbeing.

## Premenstrual Dysphoric Disorder - Indicators, Causes & Triggers (PreDDICT) Assessment

Developed in 2022, this assessment was developed specifically for individuals experiencing Premenstrual Dysphoric Disorder (PMDD) or severe Premenstrual Syndrome (PMS). Self-completed by participants through open recruitment (e.g. social media, newsletters), this assessment was administered over an extended period with participants completing an initial baseline assessment, followed by 80-days of mood diaries, and a further followup assessment upon completion. Biological (saliva) samples were also collected for a subset of eligible participants. This assessment collected details about the participants demographics, psychiatric history, PMDD/ PMS experiences, medication, menstrual cycle, pregnancy, treatments, physical health, and longitudinal mood monitoring. 


## Genetic Architecture Of Sex Steroid-related Psychiatric Disorders (GASSP) Assessment

Developed in 2023 following grant funding from the European Research Council (ERC), the Genetic Architecture Of Sex Steroid-related Psychiatric Disorders (GASSP) project is the first molecular genetic study of the psychiatric sensitivity to sex hormone changes. Also known as the Mums and Mental Health (MAM) study, GASSP aimed to recruit participants with psychiatric disorders (e.g. Post-partum Psychosis) which are temporally related to changes in sex hormones. This study also collected biological (saliva) samples for a subset of eligible participants. This assessment collected details about the participants demographics, psychiatric history, episodes of serious mental illness, treatments, pregnancy, and menstrual health.

# EARLY INTERVENTION SERVICE (EIS) ASSESSMENTS

Focussing primarily on individuals from Early Intervention Services (EIS) within the NHS, these assessments were developed to assess individuals with a psychosis (or related) diagnosis. 

## Early Intervention Services (EIS) Assessment

Developed in 2022, this assessment was developed utilising many of the questions and standardised scales used in other NCMH assessments. Recruiting exclusively through systematic methods, researchers from NHS sites containing early intervention services would administer this assessment to individuals with psychosis (or related diagnoses) following admission. This assessment was split into two sections, the first (basic/ baseline assessment) being administered by a researcher in the EIS, followed by a followup (adult questionnaire) being sent to participants by email following the completion of the baseline assessment. The followup assessment was completed in the participants own time, typically at home. These assessments collected details about the participants demographics, psychiatric history, illness onset, family psychiatric history, medication and treatments, substance use, life events/ trauma experiences, mania symptoms, psychosis symptoms, and sleep quality. 

```{r, echo = FALSE}

eis <- read.csv("../Individual_Surveys/Early Intervention Services (EIS) Assessment/Early Intervention Services (EIS) Assessment.csv", fileEncoding = "latin1")

```

**Total Variables**: `r nrow(eis %>% group_by(new_variable_name) %>% slice(1))`
<br>**Total Participants**: 238
<br>**Recruitment Dates**: Mar 2022 - Mar 2025
<br>**Recruitment Method**: Participant Self-completed and Researcher Administered
<br>**Data Collection Method**: Online (REDCap)

## Early Intervention Services (EIS) Objective Ratings Form (ORF)

Developed in 2022, this assessment was used alongside the **Early Intervention Services (EIS) Assessment**. The Objective Ratings Form (ORF) was used by researchers to validate participant responses to questions relating to symptomatology. This assessment was not completed for all participants, only those where a discrepancy was identified between the participants self-reported responses to questions and the researchers' observations whilst the participant was admitted to the early intervention service. This assessment collected details about the participants psychiatric history, medication and treatments, substance use, and clinical measures of psychosis symptomatology.

# MATERNAL WELLBEING, MENTAL HEALTH, AND LIFE EVENTS (MWMHLE) ASSESSMENTS

First developed in 2021, the **Maternal Wellbeing, Mental Health, and Life Events (MWMHLE)** study was developed to thoroughly investigate the experiences of currently pregnant and post-partum mothers. Two versions of the study have been developed to-date, both studying participants over a 12-month period through a self-completed baseline assessment and multiple followup assessments during this time. Both assessments are very detailed and covered a large scope of questions, the second version differing slightly in content and structure from the first.

## MWMHLE (v1)

The first version (v1) of the MWMHLE assessment was split into six individual surveys on our survey provider (Alchemer). This consisted of two baseline assessments and four followup assessments, all the details will be highlighted in the sections below. 

### MWMHLE (v1) Baseline (Open)

```{r, echo = FALSE}

mwmhle_v1_open <- read.csv("../Individual_Surveys/MWMHLE (v1) Baseline (Open)/MWMHLE (v1) Baseline (Open).csv", fileEncoding = "latin1")

```

This baseline assessment was administered to a large number of participants through open recruitment (e.g. social media, newsletters, NCMH website). This collected details about the participants demographics, pregnancy status, attachment, physical health, childbirth experiences, post-partum bonding, child sleeping behaviours, life events/ trauma experiences, social support, depression and anxiety symptoms, treatments, and psychiatric history. Some included questions differed depending on the participants pregnancy status (i.e. if they were post-partum the participant received additional questions compared to those who were currently pregnant).

**Total Variables**: `r nrow(mwmhle_v1_open %>% group_by(new_variable_name) %>% slice(1))`
<br>**Total Participants**: 642

<br>**Data Collection Method**: Online (Alchemer) 
<br>**Status**: Closed 
<br>**Principal Investigator**: Prof. Ian Jones 
<br>**Standardised Scales Included**: MAAS, IIQ, CEQ, PBQ, BISQ, PTGI, ACE, ITQ, MSPSS, PHQ-9, GAD-7

## MWMHLE (v2)

The second version (v2) of the MWMHLE assessment differed from the first as it was hosted on a different survey platform - REDCap - and has been condensed into a single dataset rather than multiple. The overall structure of the survey is similar to the previous version, however there are less followup assessments in the current version, as well as the content of the assessment differing slightly; this version being more condensed and user-friendly. 

```{r, echo = FALSE}

mwmhle_v2 <- read.csv("../Individual_Surveys/MWMHLE (v2)/MWMHLE (v2).csv", fileEncoding = "latin1")

```

Due to the large size of this dataset, as well as there being multiple followups and a baseline condensed into a single dataset, below is a breakdown of the data included. Note, when using the data dictionary below, utilise the variables suffixed **_timestamp** (e.g. mwmhle_basic_assessment_timestamp); these will indicate the start of a new survey, i.e. the baseline and followups. 

BASELINE: Administered to participants through two recruitment streams, either open (e.g. social media, newsletters, NCMH website) or systematic (participants were signposted to the study at NHS healthboards/ sites) methods. Regardless of recruitment method, the content of the baseline assessment was identical. This collected details about the participants demographics, pregnancy status, fertility, attachment, post-labour experiences, experiences during childbirth, life events/ trauma experiences, post-partum bonding, child sleeping behaviours, physical health, psychiatric history, treatments, services accessed, social support, anxiety and depression symptoms, emotion regulation, relationships, and self-compassion. Some included questions differed depending on the participants pregnancy status (i.e. if they were post-partum the participant received additional questions compared to those who were currently pregnant).

1-MONTH FOLLOWUP: Administered only to participants who stated they were pregnant during the baseline assessment, this followup assessment was automatically sent to participants 1-month after their stated pregnancy due date - captured on the baseline assessment - via email. This collected details about the participants childbirth experiences, life events/ trauma experiences, bonding, child sleeping behaviours, services accessed, social support, anxiety and depression symptoms, resilience, and self-compassion.  

6-MONTH FOLLOWUP: Administered to participants 6-months after the completion of the baseline assessment, this followup was automatically sent to participants via email. This collected details about the participants social support, services accessed, life events/ trauma experiences, depression and anxiety symptoms, resilience, emotion regulation, self-compassion, and borderline personality disorder symptoms.

12-MONTH FOLLOWUP: Administered to participants 12-months after the completion of the baseline assessment, this followup was automatically sent to participants via email. This assessment is identical to the 6-month followup and collected details about the participants social support, services accessed, life events/ trauma experiences, depression and anxiety symptoms, resilience, emotion regulation, self-compassion, and borderline personality disorder symptoms.

**Total Variables**: `r nrow(mwmhle_v2 %>% group_by(new_variable_name) %>% slice(1))`
<br>**Total Participants**: 720+
<br>**Recruitment Dates**: Jan 2024 - Present
<br>**Recruitment Method**: Participant Self-completed 
<br>**Data Collection Method**: Online (REDCap) 
<br>**Status**: Open 
<br>**Principal Investigator**: Dr. Cerith Waters
<br>**Standardised Scales Included**: MAAS, CEQ, PTGI, PBQ, BISQ, ACE, ITQ, MSPSS, PHQ-9, GAD-7, DERS-SF, ECR-S, SCS-SF, CD-RISC-10, LEC-5, BPS

# TRAUMA ASSESSMENTS

Since 2016, NCMH has been conducting research into individuals experiencing various forms of trauma, including Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD), Complex Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (CPTSD), childhood trauma, and other major life events. Various assessments have been developed and administered over time, each of which focussing on different traumatic experiences, with both researcher-led and participant self-completed assessments being administered. 

## PTSD Registry Interview (v5a)

```{r, echo = FALSE}

ptsd_int_v5a <- read.csv("../Individual_Surveys/PTSD Registry Interview (v5a)/PTSD Registry Interview (v5a).csv")

```

Administered to a small number of participants, this researcher-led structured clinical assessment aimed to collect detailed information about a participants' traumatic experiences and identify if their symptoms were concordant with a diagnosis of PTSD/ CPTSD. This assessment collected details about the participants demographics, emotional state, health and wellbeing, life events/ trauma experiences, trauma symptoms, PTSD and CPTSD diagnoses, and borderline personality disorder diagnosis. 

**Total Variables**: `r nrow(ptsd_int_v5a %>% group_by(new_variable_name) %>% slice(1))` 
<br>**Total Participants**: 76
<br>**Recruitment Dates**: Sep 2017 - Sep 2019
<br>**Recruitment Method**: Offline (FORMIC)
<br>**Data Collection Method**: Researcher Administered
<br>**Status**: Closed 
<br>**Principal Investigator**: Prof. Ian Jones
<br>**Standardised Scales Included**: LEC-5, CAPS-5

# STUDENT COHORT ASSESSMENTS

Initially developed in 2018, the NCMH student cohort has been expanding continually up until the present day. Between 2018 and 2020 the student-focussed assessments were developed and administered exclusively by NCMH. In 2022, NCMH partnered with the U-Flourish Nurture-U group (https://www.nurtureuniversity.co.uk/), resulting a new assessment being developed which was to be administered in different universities across the UK (incl. Cardiff, Southampton, Newcastle, Oxford, King's College London, and Exeter Universities) and datasets collated for research purposes. Multiple iterations of these assessments were developed with both baseline and followup assessments changing from year to year.

## Student Health and Wellbeing Study (2019)

```{r, echo = FALSE}

alch_ss_2019 <- read.csv("../Individual_Surveys/Student Health and Wellbeing Study (2019)/Student Health and Wellbeing Study (2019).csv")

```

This assessment was administered to a large number of participants through open recruitment (e.g. social media, newsletters, NCMH website). This assessment was similar to the **NCMH Brief Assessment** but adapted to a student population; it collected details about the participants demographics, student status, psychiatric history, treatments, physical health, mood and wellbeing, depression and anxiety symptoms, and support services accessed.

# UKMINDS

In collaboration with Akrivia Health (https://akriviahealth.com/), NCMH recruited a large number of participants with neuropsychiatric or neurodegenerative conditions for extensive phenotypic and genotypic data collection; the project was known as **UKMINDS**. Alongside the datasets mentioned here, the project greatly emphasised the collection of biomarker samples (i.e. DNA, RNA, Plasma, PBMC, and Serum) for sequencing and analysis. Two primary cohorts were established for this study, individuals with mood and psychosis diagnoses (neuropsychiatric cohort) and those with dementia and cognitive impairments (neurodegenerative cohort), each of which had different baseline assessments and Adult Questionnaires (AQs). 

## UKMINDS Mood and Psychosis Baseline

```{r, echo = FALSE}

ukm_base_moodpsych <- read.csv("../Individual_Surveys/UKMINDS Mood and Psychosis Baseline/UKMINDS Mood and Psychosis Baseline.csv", fileEncoding = "latin1")

```

This assessment was administered to the majority of participants recruited into the study; those with a mood and/ or psychosis (neuropsychiatric) diagnosis. All recruitment originated from NHS healthboards/ sites or NCMH Senior Psychology Assistants (SPAs). This collected details about the participants demographics, psychiatric history, psychosis symptoms, depression symptoms, bipolar symptoms, treatments, physical health, and intelligence.

**Total Variables**: `r nrow(ukm_base_moodpsych %>% group_by(new_variable_name) %>% slice(1))`
<br>**Total Participants**: 1647
<br>**Recruitment Dates**: Jan 2023 - Aug 2024
<br>**Recruitment Method**: Researcher Administered 
<br>**Data Collection Method**: Online (SmartSurvey) 
<br>**Status**: Closed
<br>**Principal Investigator**: Prof. James Walters 
<br>**Standardised Scales Included**: PHQ-9, GAD-7, NART

Administered to all participants who completed the **UKMINDS Mood and Psychosis Baseline Assessment**, the Adult Questionnaire (AQ) was a self-completed assessment which participants often completed in their own time. Most AQs were emailed to participants following the completion of the baseline assessment, however some were sent to participants' home address for completion in paper form; these forms were then input on SmartSurvey by an NCMH staff member. This collected details about the participants alcohol use, life events/ trauma experiences, disabilities, and experiences of anhedonia.

## UKMINDS Dementia and Cognitive Impairment Adult Questionnaire (AQ)

```{r, echo = FALSE}

```

Administered only to participants who were deemed to have appropriate capacity to complete the Adult Questionnaire (AQ) following the completion of the **UKMINDS Dementia and Cognitive Impairment Baseline Assessment**. The AQ was a self-completed assessment which participants often completed in their own time. Most AQs were emailed to participants following the completion of the baseline assessment, however some were sent to participants' home address for completion in paper form; these forms were then input on SmartSurvey by an NCMH staff member. This collected details about the participants quality of life, anxiety and depression symptoms, and sleep quality. 

Note: There were two versions of the EuroQol-5D Assessment (EQ-5D-5L and EQ-5D-3L) included in this assessment. This was an error during the design process that was not detected until the study was actively recruiting (~20/04/2024). Once the error was detected, the EQ-5D-3L was hidden from participant view on SmartSurvey so only the EQ-5D-5L could be completed.

# SLEEP ASSESSMENTS

Developed in 2016, various sleep interviews and questionnaires were developed to assess participants sleep quality and factors affecting their sleep. Alongside researcher-led interviews and participants self-completed questionnaires, participants also wore Actigraphy devices for a period of time to objectively measure their sleeping patterns.

# COVID-19 ASSESSMENTS

Developed in 2020, the COVID-19 assessments were created as a direct result of the COVID-19 pandemic. Administered to a large proportion of the existing NCMH cohort - as well as new participants through open recruitment - multiple assessments were developed focussing on topical research areas. Multiple baseline assessments were administered, the content of which largely borrowed from the **NCMH Brief Assessment Online** with additional questions focussing on COVID-19 being included. Three followup assessments were administered to all participants completing a baseline, each followup specialising in different research topics.

# NEURODEVELOPMENTAL ASSESSMENTS

NCMH has historically undertaken sub-projects focussing on neurodevelopmental conditions such as Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) and Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD). These projects have all been undertaken by co-Principal Investigators affiliated with NCMH.

## Psychiatric Comorbidity in ASD

```{r, echo = FALSE}

comorbid_asd <- read.csv("../Individual_Surveys/Psychiatric Comorbidity in ASD/Psychiatric Comorbidity in ASD.csv", fileEncoding = "latin1")

```

Developed sometime between 2017-2020, this Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD)-focussed assessment was developed using the **Autism Spectrum Quotient 50-Item (AQ-50)**, a standardised scale used to identify autistic traits in adults. This assessment was specifically developed for a research project led by Dr Jack Underwood, and recruited participants from the NCMH cohort who had existing self-reported diagnoses of ASD or Autism. This assessment collected details about the participants ASD traits as well as social responsiveness, experiences of migraines, and anxiety and depression symptoms. 

**Total Variables**: `r nrow(comorbid_asd %>% group_by(new_variable_name) %>% slice(1))` 
<br>**Total Participants**: 123
<br>**Recruitment Dates**: Information Unavailable
<br>**Recruitment Method**: Offline (FORMIC)
<br>**Data Collection Method**: Participant Self-completed
<br>**Status**: Closed 
<br>**Principal Investigator**: Dr. Jack Underwood
<br>**Standardised Scales Included**: AQ, SRS-2, ID Migraine, HADS

```{r, echo = FALSE}

# CSV FILE
csv_button(
  file_path = "../Individual_Surveys/Psychiatric Comorbidity in ASD/Psychiatric Comorbidity in ASD.csv",

  ext = ".csv"
)

  file_path = "../Individual_Surveys/Psychiatric Comorbidity in ASD/Psychiatric Comorbidity in ASD.pdf",

  ext = ".pdf"
)

```

## ADHD Survey

```{r, echo = FALSE}

adhd <- read.csv("../Individual_Surveys/ADHD Survey/ADHD Survey.csv")

```

Developed in 2021, this assessment specifically focussed on adults with a diagnosis of Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD). Due to an internal error, this assessment remained active for a number of years after its proposed closure date, resulting in recruitment extending past 2021-2022. This assessment collected details about the participants demographics, psychiatric history, medication use, children, strengths and difficulties, ADHD symptoms in children, and impact of COVID-19.

**Total Variables**: `r nrow(adhd %>% group_by(new_variable_name) %>% slice(1))`
<br>**Total Participants**: 136 
<br>**Recruitment Dates**: Mar 2021 - May 2026 
<br>**Recruitment Method**: Participant Self-completed
<br>**Data Collection Method**: Online (Alchemer) 
<br>**Status**: Closed
<br>**Principal Investigator**: Prof. Anita Thaper
<br>**Standardised Scales Included**: SDQ
